document_title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) — Revamped Operational Guidelines (2023)
text: [Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

document_title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) — Revamped Operational Guidelines (2023)
text: [Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Sum Insured (SI) Calculation: The Sum Insured per hectare for both loanee and non-loanee farmers is equal to the Scale of Finance (SoF) as decided by the District Level Technical Committee (DLTC) or notified area Threshold Yield multiplied by the Minimum Support Price (MSP), reaching 100% of the full economic value without any upper reduction capping.

document_title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) — Revamped Operational Guidelines (2023)
text: [Maximum Insurance Charges (Premium) Payable by Farmer] Important Rule on Qualification and Basis: In all three categories of Table 1, the stated percentage (2.0% for Kharif food grain and oilseed crops, 1.5% for Rabi food grain and oilseed crops, and 5.0% for annual commercial and annual horticultural crops) is a maximum ceiling expressed as a percentage of Sum Insured (SI), subject to the mandatory qualification 'or Actuarial rate, whichever is less'. If the bidding actuarial rate for a crop is lower than the prescribed ceiling (for example, 1.2% for a Kharif food grain), the farmer pays the lower actuarial rate (1.2%), not 2.0%.

document_title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) — Revamped Operational Guidelines (2023)
text: [Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Standard Enrolment Cut-Off Dates: Unless specifically varied by State notification within the permissible window, the standard final cut-off date for farmer enrolment and premium debit is 31st July for the Kharif season and 31st December for the Rabi season.

document_title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) — Revamped Operational Guidelines (2023)
section: Section XIX (Clause 19.3 - CCE & Outreach Distractor Paragraph)
text: [Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Operational Sampling and Outreach Benchmarks: For estimation of crop yield at the Gram Panchayat (Insurance Unit) level, a minimum of 4 Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) are mandatory for major crops, and 8 CCEs are required at the Mandal/Taluka level. Under the National Crop Insurance Portal outreach drive (Krishi Rakshak Helpline 14447), field agencies target at least 30% participation from women cultivators and small/marginal farmers holding less than 2.0 hectares of operational land, with digital village camps covering 5% of high-priority blocks each week. (Note: The 30% women outreach target, 2.0 hectares small-farmer landholding threshold, and 5% weekly block camp coverage are administrative outreach targets, NOT farmer insurance premium rates.)

document_title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) — Operational Guidelines (2016 Historical Edition)
text: [Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana ? Operational Guidelines (2016 Original Edition, Effective 2016-04-01 to 2020-03-31)] Historical Compulsory Enrolment Rule (2016-2020): Under the 2016 Operational Guidelines (effective from Kharif 2016, 2016-04-01 until superseded by the Revamped Guidelines on 2020-03-31), PMFBY enrolment was 100% compulsory (mandatory) for all loanee farmers availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations (SAO) credit / Kisan Credit Card (KCC) loans for notified crops, and voluntary only for non-loanee farmers.

document_title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) — Official Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
text: [Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) ? Official Frequently Asked Questions (Undated Portal Document)] Q1: What is the premium rate payable by farmers under PMFBY? Answer: Under PMFBY, farmers pay a uniform maximum premium of 2.0% of Sum Insured (or Actuarial rate, whichever is less) for all Kharif food grain and oilseed crops; 1.5% of Sum Insured (or Actuarial rate, whichever is less) for all Rabi food grain and oilseed crops; and 5.0% of Sum Insured (or Actuarial rate, whichever is less) for Annual Commercial and Annual Horticultural crops.

document_title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) — Official Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
text: [Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) ? Official Frequently Asked Questions (Undated Portal Document)] Q4: Within how many hours must a farmer report localized crop loss or post-harvest damage? Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Post-harvest losses are covered for a maximum period of 14 days (2 weeks) from harvesting for crops left in cut-and-spread condition in the field for drying.

document_title: PIB Press Release PRID=2197713 — Criteria for Assessing Losses under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana
text: [Criteria for Assessing Losses under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (Published 12 DEC 2025)] Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India (Release Date: 2025-12-12, PRID=2197713). Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is voluntary for States as well as farmers and provides comprehensive risk insurance from pre-sowing to post-harvest stages against non-preventable natural risks.

document_title: PIB Press Release PRID=2197713 — Criteria for Assessing Losses under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana
section: PIB Release PRID=2197713 (Para 3 - Wild Animal Attack Add-on Cover)
text: [Criteria for Assessing Losses under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (Published 12 DEC 2025)] Wild Animal Attack Add-on Cover: Losses caused by wild animal attacks were historically excluded from basic cover. States have been permitted to notify wild animal attack as an add-on cover based on individual assessment, implemented 100.0% at the cost of the respective State Government (0.0% Central Government subsidy liability for wild animal add-on cover). A technical committee submitted Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for wild animal attack loss assessment and localized inundation for paddy crops.

document_title: PIB Press Release PRID=2197713 — Criteria for Assessing Losses under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana
section: PIB Release PRID=2197713 (Para 4 - Scope & Versioning Limitation)
text: [Criteria for Assessing Losses under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (Published 12 DEC 2025)] Scope and Versioning Notice: This December 2025 PIB press release (PRID=2197713, published 2025-12-12) announces loss-assessment SOP modalities for wild animal attacks and hydrophilic crop (paddy, jute, mesta, sugarcane) inundation. It does NOT publish a complete revised 2025/2026 Operational Guidelines text or specify an effective date or revised farmer premium rate table.

document_title: PMFBY Official Portal — Scheme Overview Snapshot
text: [Scheme Overview] Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) provides comprehensive crop insurance coverage against non-preventable natural risks from pre-sowing to post-harvest. Enrolment is voluntary for all farmers.

document_title: PMFBY Official Portal — Scheme Overview Snapshot
text: [Farmer Premium Summary (Portal Snapshot)] Kharif Food Grains and Oilseeds: 2.0% of Sum Insured (or Actuarial rate, whichever is less). Rabi Food Grains and Oilseeds: 1.5% of Sum Insured (or Actuarial rate, whichever is less). Annual Commercial and Horticultural Crops: 5.0% of Sum Insured (or Actuarial rate, whichever is less).

document_title: Unofficial Working Group Draft on Perennial Horticulture and Spice Crop Rates
text: [Unofficial Working Group Draft on Perennial Horticulture and Spice Crop Rates (Unverified Provenance)] UNVERIFIED PROPOSAL: This unsigned working draft proposes reducing the maximum farmer premium for perennial horticultural crops to 3.5% of Sum Insured and reclassifying seed spices (coriander, cumin, fennel) at 2.0% instead of the 5.0% commercial crop rate. WARNING: This document has not been notified or verified by the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and must not be used as trusted evidence.
